notes:
Inbound SMB lead from self-serve sign-up; small support-focused startup building an in-app assistant for SMEs. Primary ask: urgent help to lower token costs during trial and early production. Specific asks: 1) batching/caching best practices for hosted API (they saw high per-token spend on bursts), 2) guidance on prompt compression and removing redundant instructions, 3) a token usage audit + quick wins they can apply without heavy infra work.

Context/actions: trial account started 2026-02-12 with 10k credits. Instrumented basic telemetry (requests, tokens) via SDK. They report average session 1200 tokens (prompt+resp) and want to target <=600 tokens by compressing context and using prefix caching. Latency SLO: ~<250ms p50, can tolerate p95 up to 600ms for UI flows. Throughput: typically 2-8 RPS, spikes to ~20 RPS during support ticket batches. Cost sensitivity: "need to get below $2k/mo at 10k users" - they expect high growth but limited runway.

Quote from onboarding call: "We love the API ergonomics; just show us where tokens are bleeding out and what to change today."

Security: SOC2 posture required for customer-facing support logs; need SSO for admin users. No air-gapped / on-prem requirement.

Suggested Redwood playbook so far: token audit export (we asked for raw request logs), set up continuous prefix caching for repeated KB prompts, recommend 8-16 token-level prompt compression heuristics, suggest batching for backend bulk-print/export workflows, and a follow-up 30m technical session to review audit output.

AE notes: friendly, pragmatic founders (CTO = former backend eng). Will likely go paid if we show 20-40% cost reduction in 2 weeks. Priorities: low-effort wins first (prompt trimming, caching), then policy-driven batching for background jobs.
